A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, and their complete main texts and appendices were inspected. Some Hausa hooked letters appear blank in v2 in both extraction and two local renderers, limiting exact character-level comparison of examples. The numerical tables and remaining substantive content support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original correction-model results in Table 1, noise-distribution analysis, and a native-speaker evaluation of 500 predictions in Section 4.2.

after.justification: V2 reports original correction, out-of-domain, classification, translation, and instruction-following experiments in Tables 2–6, alongside human evaluation.

M1.justification: V2 extends the correction framework with instruction-formatted fine-tuning of the Llama-based N-ATLaS causal model, documented in Section 4 and Appendices A and D. This is a limited procedural extension of v1's sequence-to-sequence setup. The synthetic-noise operations and their probabilities remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds professionally translated MultiplEYE texts for out-of-domain correction and genre classification, NaijaSenti sentiment evaluation, FLORES+ Hausa-to-English translation, and MasakhaNER/IrokoBench tasks covering NER, question answering, mathematics, and inference. Its reported corpus composition also omits the Bible and Tanzil sources included in v1.

E2.justification: The main correction comparison adds N-ATLaS, Cheetah, and GPT-5.1, while removing the AfriTEVA-Large and Opus-MT result rows present in v1 Table 1. The original noisy-input comparator continues as Copy Baseline; its renamed row is not a new comparison method.

E3.justification: V2 reports revised corpus counts, overlap filtering, Jensen–Shannon distance for calibration, stratified five-fold genre evaluation, and original/noisy/clean downstream comparisons with task-specific metrics. New settings include 997 FLORES+ sentence pairs and a separate two-epoch N-ATLaS configuration reserving 5% for validation. The original three-epoch sequence-to-sequence defaults remain in Appendix A.

E4.justification: V2 adds contamination analysis finding 56 approximate overlaps with less than 0.001 metric impact, out-of-domain generalization tests, quantitative calibration agreement, AfriTeVA paraphrasing examples, and task-specific noise/recovery analyses. V1's distribution comparison, 500-prediction human evaluation, and five appendix cases are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V1 provides point estimates without repeated-run uncertainty. V2 adds three GPT-5.1 prompting runs with average scores reported ±0.001, unspecified multiple N-ATLaS runs with ±0.001 reporting, and standard deviations for five-fold genre classification. The correction-run uncertainty statistic and N-ATLaS run count remain incompletely specified.

E6.justification: Correction scores change beyond rounding: M2M100 BLEU changes from 0.8593 to 0.853 under revised data/filtering, so this is not an established same-setting decline. V2 Table 2 places N-ATLaS first on BLEU, F1, and CER, with M2M100 leading METEOR and tying WER. New results include Google Translate BLEU improving from 33.07 on noisy input to 35.02 after cleaning, while AfriMGSM accuracy remains 49. The reported 500-sample human outcomes are unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theoretical results or proofs. V2 states the standard Jensen–Shannon distance formula to document an empirical calibration metric; this does not introduce new mathematical reasoning or a novel formal definition.

C1.justification: V1's central empirical contribution concerns intrinsic correction quality. V2 explicitly claims practical downstream benefits and emphasizes a small M2M100 model performing comparably to an 8B model. The introduction also adds a first-tools-for-Hausa novelty claim, substantially expanding the contribution framing.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving pretraining-task alignment, paraphrasing, contamination, and accuracy/compute tradeoffs. Downstream discussion distinguishes partial recovery from failures, including unrecovered mathematics performance and sensitivity to entity boundaries. Limitations shift from absent downstream validation toward genre-mismatched synthetic noise, automatic-metric biases, and incomplete recovery of meaning.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents lexicon-based error identification, length buckets, DBSCAN parameters, and iterative noise calibration; these details do not establish that the existing calibration procedure changed. It also supplies N-ATLaS optimization settings, correction/training/translation prompts in Appendices C–E, and an explicit code/data repository link. Original sequence-to-sequence hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around African NLP resources, specialized language models, and downstream benchmarks, including Cheetah, N-ATLaS, MasakhaNER, IrokoBench, and MultiplEYE. It removes the generic rule-based/statistical/neural correction survey and adds explicit first-tool positioning. Publication updates to retained works are not substantive additions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusions are extensively revised. Data preparation and correction models become separate main sections, results absorb discussion, and downstream evaluation receives its own section. Appendix noise material moves into the main text, while examples move from Appendix D to B and new prompt appendices follow.

P2.justification: V2 adds four results tables and a genre-distribution figure, restructures the correction table with parameter counts and shaded model rows, and redraws and relocates the calibration plot. The unchanged noise-probability table moves into the main text. Typography and layout change throughout; missing Hausa glyphs impair portions of v2's examples.

improvement.justification: V1 explicitly deferred downstream validation; v2 directly tests practical effects across several tasks and reports both recoveries and failures. Together with out-of-domain and contamination checks, these experiments substantially strengthen evidence about when correction helps. Expanded implementation documentation also improves reproducibility. Ranking prose that conflicts with Table 2 and missing Hausa glyphs remain material defects, but the added validation resolves an important deficiency of v1 and outweighs those shortcomings.
